81d9b8125438d996: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 16 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the affected areas were in Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Selangor, Johor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Negri Sembilan recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading nationwide, with Nilai registering 162, followed by Seremban (156) and Port Dickson (151).
Melaka also registered unhealthy readings, with Bukit Rambai recording 160, Bandaraya Melaka (148) and Alor Gajah (101).
Selangor saw five areas affected, led by Klang (156), Johan Setia (155), Petaling Jaya (153), Shah Alam (152) and Banting (136).
Johor's affected locations were Tangkak (153) and Pasir Gudang (109).
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur recorded unhealthy readings in Batu Muda (152) and Cheras (143), while Putrajaya registered 141.
APIMS data also showed that 49 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings.
Three areas recorded good air quality, namely Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (48), Kimanis (39) and Limbang (35).
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.
235b93af2580a408: PETALING JAYA: The deregistration of Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaves PAS free to pursue cooperation with Umno, says the Islamic party's spiritual leader Hashim Jasin.
He said the move would not hurt PAS but would affect Bersatu the most, as it had long relied on PAS’s strength in PN, Utusan Malaysia reported.
"PAS can focus on cooperating with Umno, which the people have long awaited.
"A PAS-Umno coalition or cooperation will give a big advantage in the 16th general election," he said, adding that PAS would find it "easier" to win the general election under such an arrangement.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS) deregistered PN after finding that the coalition’s explanation failed to address the grounds stated in an earlier notice.
The RoS acted on a complaint by Bersatu, which alleged that it was denied the right to attend, speak and vote at a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16.
The deregistration came ahead of a High Court hearing today on PN’s application to quash a show-cause notice and a separate notice suspending the coalition’s activities.
The deregistration means PN cannot use its logo in the upcoming Melaka polls, although its component parties may contest under their own emblems.

Bersatu has described the deregistration as evidence of PAS’s failure to manage the coalition democratically and transparently, while PAS has called it an attempt to pre-empt the court and weaken the opposition ahead of the Melaka election.
069d804a254c3da2: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 22 — The row of red lanterns dangling on a wire. The white-washed walls of 19th century pre-war Chinese shophouses. The tall wooden window shutters.
And within one of these shophouses, some of the best coffee you’d taste in Johor Bahru.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A small flat white and a filter coffee at Sweet Blossom.

This is Jalan Tan Hiok Nee, one of the city’s heritage enclaves. I confess I haven’t been back in a decade or so, but I remember dropping by whenever I was in the area, especially for Hiap Joo Bakery’s signature banana cake, baked using a wood fire oven.
Much has changed since then. Hiap Joo still draws a queue of customers eager for their banana cake, but now they can enjoy it with an espresso or a freshly brewed pour over coffee too.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Barista and bags of coffee beans at Sweet Blossom.
Just a minute’s walk from the stalwart bakery is Sweet Blossom Coffee - Heritage Street. This is the second outlet by owner Ang Yeesiang; he opened his first café 11 years ago in Taman Pelangi.

While that original shop now functions as the Sweet Blossom HQ and roastery, with clientele made up of regulars, the Jalan Tan Hiok Nee branch attracts more tourists and passers-by looking for a caffeine fix.
Ang remembers I prefer a small flat white; for my friend, a local, he suggests a filter coffee made with Peruvian beans.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Don’t miss the gelato at Ancora Gelato & Bakery.
Hailing from Doña Fica by Nixer Ordoñez Gómez, the extended fermentation washed coffee has jammy plum and rich raspberry notes and a scent reminiscent of lemongrass.
Ask the barista for recommendations if you’d like to purchase a bag of coffee beans to bring home. They also offer soft serve ice cream and affogato for those who crave something cool.

Next we are off to Jalan Dhoby, which runs parallel to Jalan Tan Hiok Nee. Together they form the bulk of what is known as Johor Bahru’s heritage hub, now reinvigorated with a fresh coat of paint and tourist-oriented shops.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Cups of Ancora’s gelato.
The latter runs the gamut from independent cafés, art galleries, retro thrift shops and, given our climate, more ice cream purveyors than one might expect given the neighbourhood’s size.
My friend has his favourite; he says we can’t visit the hub and miss the gelato at Ancora Gelato & Bakery.

The shop itself is clean and minimalist; expect pristine white walls and gleaming metal tubs of ice cream. Arranged neatly along the front counter, each tub offers a different flavour of gelato or sorbet.
There are classics such as strawberry and dark chocolate; nutty hits like pistachio, black sesame and hazelnut chocolate; as well as fruity sorbets, from mango passion fruit to lemon lemongrass.
There is even a tea-centric series of gelato, from the more common Earl Grey and Thai milk tea to more delicate concoctions such as osmanthus oolong, pu’er milk tea and jasmine with green grape.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Flowers in the Window, an all-day brunch and fusion café.
Share your personal preferences with the friendly staff and they will be more happy to suggest flavours, offering sample spoons to try and explaining the flavour profiles of each.
Taste the Mediterranean with a cup of their olive oil and lemon basil ice creams; Japanese accents are represented by matcha and hojicha.

Some of the more interesting flavours include tofu (reminds me of a light, extra creamy tau foo fa), Japanese cucumber (which, believe it or not, isn’t a sorbet but a gelato — and somehow works, each scoop refreshing and revelatory).
After this little pick-me-up, it’s time for something savoury and substantial. We cross the street to Flowers in the Window, an all-day brunch and fusion café.

The décor caters to visitors seeking a certain aesthetic: both verdant (creeping vines along the walls, cacti and hanging ferns) and vintage (repurposed old shop signboards, random collectibles and old records).

Which often means the menu is simply an afterthought; a few pretty plates to photograph to upload on the socials later. Fortunately that isn’t the case at Flowers in the Window, where carefully curated offerings tempt us mercilessly.

In the end, we decide on their Mexican Breakfast and Lotus Chips Salmon Bowl; our selection criteria revolving around the amount of protein and fibre, which I reckon is as good an ordering strategy as any.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Mexican Breakfast at Flowers in the Window

The Mexican Breakfast employs a tortilla as the canvas, then arranges spicy chicken chorizo (almost stew like), cool Cheddar, creamy avocado and a sunny-side-up egg in a colourful layer. Nachos and salsa on the side add a welcome crunch and a bright, tangy kick.

Avocado makes another appearance in the Lotus Chips Salmon Bowl; it is de rigueur for brunch staples, no? Here it is accompanied by chunks of salmon, pan-seared until its exterior develops a lovely crust, while the flakes of flesh remain tender and moist.

Then there is the supporting cast – a smooth pea mash, sweet roasted pumpkin, a soft-boiled egg – and the crowning glory of fried lotus chips, light and crisp. A nutty peanut dressing ties the ingredients together.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Lotus Chips Salmon Bowl at Flowers in the Window.
Now this is what I call a meal: crunchy and creamy, smokey and savoury. All the flavours and textures you could want, and maybe a little more?
Which is perhaps the biggest surprise of my return to Jalan Tan Hiok Nee and Jalan Dhoby after so many years away.
These heritage streets have changed, sure. A bit gentrified, there’s no denying that. But also how you can now have a globe-trotting adventure here, all within a few minutes walk. Bon appétit!

faf333ad923f6a18: AUSTIN: Max Verstappen is set to be a party-pooper this weekend as he seeks to delay Kimi Antonelli's title celebrations by notching a third consecutive win with another triumph at the United States Grand Prix.

Red Bull's four-time world champion won both the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and then the Singapore Grand Prix to emerge as a leading contender for more success just when Mercedes' precocious 20-year-old Italian moved within reach of the title.

The 29-year-old Dutchman, who has acknowledged Antonelli's generational talent, won from pole at the Circuit of the Americas last year and is chasing a fifth win at the Texan track where Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was won five times.

But Verstappen has been reluctant to claim that Red Bull's recovery in form and results will automatically translate to more success. "It's difficult to say – I don't want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin," he said after his Singapore win.
"But the last few weekends have been great. I just take it race by race and we'll see how it goes there. It's another very different kind of track."

After a run of seven podium finishes in his last eight races, including two wins and three second places, Verstappen, 119 points adrift in fourth, may well scupper hopes that Antonelli can win and, with the stars aligning, become Italy's first champion since 1953 and the youngest in F1 history.

To seize the title in Texas, the Italian, who leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 102 points, needs to win the race and see Russell fail to finish in the top nine and Hamilton outside the top four.
Antonelli was only four years old when Sebastian Vettel took the record as youngest champion, with Red Bull, in 2010, and he knows he must stay focused and race to win, as he always does.

"I know it's very close and I know it's there, but I need to make sure I keep doing my best and go out and win and perform in my best way," he said. Italy's last champion was Alberto Ascari for Ferrari.

McLaren's deputy team principal Bradley Lord drew upon tennis when he described Antonelli's position by saying: "We're in that uncomfortable phase where you have to navigate the media with everyone saying 'you can do it – you've got first match point."

Russell's hopes of reining in Antonelli may be aided by Verstappen while Hamilton could also be a threat as he returns to one of his favourite circuits seeking a record sixth win and seventh in the United States GP.

Both Mercedes drivers will run the team's latest updates package as they go into a decisive triple-header of races in Texas, Mexico and Brazil, but it may be that Ferrari and Red Bull can steal the initiative.
These races may be run on bumpy tracks and in hot conditions that deliver unexpected results, a prospect that Verstappen has anticipated.

"From what I saw in the world endurance championship race in Austin, the track is incredibly bumpy and I will probably need to order a new spine after the weekend – or become like Robocop. It's crazy."
4c508131652db4b7: NEW YORK: Oil prices rose on Thursday as more attacks by the Houthis in Saudi Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the Kingdom.

Brent crude futures rose US$1.29, or 1.2 per cent, to US$110.11 a barrel at 00:34 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 97 cents, or 1 per cent, to US$98.12. Brent had settled largely unchanged on Wednesday, while WTI had eased 67 cents.
The US State Department plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis struck several targets on Wednesday with at least one person killed and eight more wounded at a civilian airport in Dammam, and two people killed in a drone attack on a Saudi oil field.
Explosions were also heard in Sirik in southern Iran, Iranian media reported on Wednesday, saying the nature and origin of the explosions were unknown.

On Wednesday, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself and President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.

There were at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks, Kpler data showed, while LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, reaching into the Gulf of Oman and jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers supporting regional loadings.

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday for talks on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.

US crude stocks fell by 3.06 million barrels to 412.5 million barrels last week, the US Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for an 820,000-barrel draw.
Distillate stockpiles, which include diesel and heating oil, rose 1.68 million barrels in the week to 104.3 million barrels, versus expectations for a 1.16 million-barrel drop, EIA data showed.

The Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the 1-million-barrel US emergency heating oil reserve, the Department of Energy said on Wednesday, seeking to contain prices that have surged on diesel shortages due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
eb2bcb7668ba43a1: PETALING JAYA: At 18, Khalisah Damia Abd Kadim, known as Leesya, weighs just 14kg and is bedridden due to cerebral palsy.
Unlike other teenagers her age, Leesya is unable to walk or crawl and can utter only two words: "ayah" (father) and "ibu" (mother).
She also has scoliosis, a condition involving an abnormal curvature of the spine.
Her mother, Siti Robaah Mohd Munaf, 56, said Leesya, the youngest of six siblings, had appeared healthy at birth.
"Everything changed when Leesya developed jaundice, with her bilirubin levels rising sharply on the fifth day after she was born.
"My husband and I took her to a clinic, where the doctor gave us a referral letter and asked us to take her to hospital.

"Following further examinations, doctors suspected that Leesya had cerebral palsy, and she was subsequently registered as a person with disabilities under the physical disability category," she said when met at her home in Kampung Lindungan here.
Siti Robaah admitted that she initially struggled to accept her daughter's condition, having hoped that Leesya would grow up without health problems.
"It took me some time to come to terms with what had happened. I cried, but eventually accepted it because I believe this is what God has decreed.
"Since Leesya was born, I have never heard anyone say anything hurtful about her. Everyone, including our relatives and close friends, has accepted her.

"However, Leesya is not like other teenagers her age. Many people think she is still a baby or a young child because of her small frame. Her growth began slowing down and appeared to become stunted when she was 13," she said.
Siti Robaah, a housewife, said she spent most of her time caring for Leesya and attending to her daily needs.
"My daily routine involves giving Leesya special formula milk every four hours, six times a day.
"I also have to put her on breathing support and help remove mucus from her airways using a machine at home.

"Caring for a child like this requires a great deal of patience because when Leesya becomes distressed, she vomits. She has also been admitted to hospital many times, usually because of fever or infections," she said.
Siti Robaah, who is also a stroke survivor, said she would continue caring for her daughter for as long as she lived.
"I have already reminded my husband and other children to look after Leesya if I pass away before her," she said.

Meanwhile, Leesya's brother, Mohamad Zamrin Abd Kadim, 23, who is pursuing a bachelor's degree in Computer Software Engineering in Multimedia at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, said he helped care for his sister whenever he had free time despite undergoing industrial training.
"At first, I did not really understand her condition, but as I grew older, I began to understand and realise my responsibilities.
"Whatever happens, I will take turns caring for my sister because I will never leave her alone," he said.
Mohamad Zamrin has also worked as a delivery rider for the past three years to help pay his university fees and ease his family's financial burden.

6209eb0fc2b61a39: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The achievements of GovTech Malaysia, the status of Malaysians who remain unreachable following flash floods in Nepal, and the accuracy of Malaysia’s official Air Pollutant Index (API) readings are among the key issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.

She will also seek details on the success of strategic collaborations with other ministries in improving service delivery to the public and business sector, as well as the agency’s plans to strengthen the digital government ecosystem.

Meanwhile, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the Foreign Minister for an update on Malaysians who remain unreachable following flash floods that struck Nepal’s Rasuwa district on Aug 26.

Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara) will ask the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister to explain the measures taken to ensure that official API readings remain accurate, transparent and trusted by the public.

He will also seek clarification on whether the government plans to improve the dissemination of air quality information to make it easier for the public to understand and more responsive to changing haze conditions.

Meanwhile, during the oral question session, Datuk Siti Aminah Aching (BN-Beaufort) will ask the Minister of Finance the number of pickup truck and jeep owners in Sabah who have received the additional 100-litre allocation under the BUDI Diesel initiative.
She will also seek details on assistance for owners who use the vehicles for small businesses, agricultural activities or travel to rural areas.

Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) will ask the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister for details of the enforcement outcomes under Ops Tiris Bersepadu, particularly in border areas, including the number of cases, value of leakages, seizures and arrests.

Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) will ask the Women, Family and Community Development Minister to state the number of women aged between 25 and 59 who are outside the labour force due to caregiving responsibilities, including caring for children, older persons and other family members.
She will also seek clarification on the economic value of unpaid care work to the country and when a national care economy ecosystem will be established.

The Dewan Rakyat sitting will subsequently continue with the policy-level debate on the Supply Bill 2027, following its tabling by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, on Oct 9.

According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-level debate on the 2027 Budget is scheduled from Oct 12 to 22, followed by a four-day winding-up session by the relevant ministers beginning on Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting is scheduled to run for 37 days, until Dec 8. — Bernama
e3add29b55de7457: NEW YORK: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks while weakness in communication services stocks capped gains.

SpaceX shares finished up 7.8 per cent after Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm posted its first profit as a public company. Musk said, following the report, that a merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be "a good idea," also boosting Tesla shares.

Elsewhere in earnings, Super Micro shares jumped 9.6 per cent and it was among the S&P 500's top gainers after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. The report also benefited peers HPE, which rose 3.7 per cent, and Dell, which rose 5.3 per cent.

The reports provided some reassurance to investors who have been worried about the sustainability of massive spending on AI buildouts and their profitability. The technology sector was hammered last week by a selloff in AI-linked stocks, with data center operator CoreWeave at the center of the storm.
The SpaceX news "pushes back on some of the investor worries" about AI along with some help from Super Micro, according to Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones.
Kourkafas said the reports will not "answer all the questions investors have on returns on AI investments, but it's a good start."
As a result, the S&P 500 Information Technology index finished up 1.6 per cent, the biggest gainer among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors.
"It's really a positive technology story for almost anyone that is somewhat involved in the artificial intelligence ecosystem," said Marc Dizard, chief investment officer at Huntington Bank.
"The technology market reaction has been a reaffirmation that the artificial intelligence trade is still intact," he added.
However, Dizard said sentiment can quickly shift around AI and that investors will seek reaffirmation when they monitor earnings reports from other companies.

Shares in Meta rose 3 per cent in late trading after it released its quarterly results following the regular session's close. After finishing up 3.4 per cent in the regular session, Tesla shares rose another 1.6 per cent following its report, which was also issued after the close.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 360.21 points, or 0.69 per cent, to 52,856.09, the S&P 500 gained 44.60 points, or 0.58 per cent, to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 278.04 points, or 1.05 per cent, to 26,702.86.
Within technology, one of the strongest areas was chips with a 2 per cent rally in the Philadelphia Semiconductor index, which has had a volatile month so far including an eight-session selloff.

Gains in the benchmark S&P 500 were limited however by a 1.3 per cent decline in communication services stocks. The biggest losers included telecom operators such as AT&T, which sank 6.5 per cent even as it beat third-quarter revenue and profit expectations.

The SpaceX results, along with a recent wireless spectrum purchase, fanned fears that it could become a formidable competitor in telecoms, according to Dizard. T-Mobile US shares fell 2.5 per cent and Verizon Communications lost 2.2 per cent.

Also in communications services, Netflix shares sank 5.3 per cent after the video streaming company issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for its fourth-quarter profit. Google's parent Alphabet also declined 1.6 per cent.
Abbott Laboratories shares dropped 1.9 per cent after the medical device maker cut its 2026 sales growth forecast.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.37-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 131 new highs and 221 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 2,690 stocks rose and 2,068 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.3-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 26 new 52-week highs and 3 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 53 new highs and 216 new lows.
On US exchanges roughly 16.11 billion shares changed hands compared with the 17.10 billion average for the last 20 sessions.

7c5c22f00fbb44e9: MUMBAI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that decisions regarding Ukraine's access to Starlink were up to its parent company SpaceX and Elon Musk, not the White House, comments that suggested Musk may have restricted Kyiv's access to the service.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk had ordered the slowdown of Starshield, a military-grade version of Starlink that ​Ukraine relies on to defend itself against missile attacks from Russia.

The Journal cited one person saying that SpaceX CEO Musk, president Donald Trump and White House officials discussed the matter beforehand, and two people saying that Musk and the president discussed the matter in the days after the slowdown.
"I'm not aware that we knew about this decision beforehand. But that's irrelevant," Rubio told reporters during a trip to India.
"The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how their stuff can be used and what speeds they'll allow it to be used at."
Musk and SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment.
Trump, asked by reporters on Wednesday whether Musk ordered the slowdown, said: "I don't know who did it, but I was not involved."

Reuters has cited two US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter saying the decision ultimately came from the White House. This version was also asserted by Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky, but denied by the administration.
Rubio's comments are likely to intensify concerns in Washington regarding Musk's ability to influence US foreign policy. They also represent an apparent shift in position for the administration.

Trump has previously said publicly he believed neither he nor Musk was behind the slowdown. Departing for a trip to Uzbekistan and India on Saturday, Rubio had said no one ordered the slowdown, an assertion that drew criticism from lawmakers in both parties.
"I'm not sure Zelensky knows what he's talking about, but it wasn't deliberate," Rubio said at the time.
"We have nothing to do with that. I don't – the United States, nobody ordered that Starlink speed to be slowed down. It sort of happened, but my understanding is it's been restored," Rubio said.
Senate Democrats see risks to delegation

A Senate Democratic aide said the Starshield slowdown, which occurred during an Oct 13-16 visit to Kyiv by a bipartisan US congressional delegation, put US lawmakers and staff in the group at risk, along with 230 US personnel on the ground.

Russia was now using jet-powered versions of the Shahed drones that could fly at 280 miles per hour (450km/hour) or faster, which required faster defensive drones to mount an adequate defence, the aide said.

"It's a basic math problem. If you have a 280-mph object coming towards you, you are not going to be able to counter it with something that goes 100 mph," the aide said, noting Kyiv had lost a lot of air assets the first night of the slowdown.

At the moment, problems with transmission of US data and a slowdown in transmission of security assistance meant that drones were jeopardising the ability of the staff and delegation members to get to official shelters, the aide said.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth also portrayed the Starlink cutoff as a commercial matter. No US official has publicly said, however, that they have pushed SpaceX to reverse any cutoffs.
"There are terms of service that ultimately need to be complied to, and that's where Starlink has the option to make those decisions," Hegseth said.

One significant point of confusion relates to the difference between SpaceX's Starshield and Starlink products. Starshield is essentially a military-grade version of Starlink developed for the Pentagon.
Rubio suggested on Saturday that Ukraine never had access to Starshield in the first place, while Zelensky has said that both Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine have been disrupted.

43152cf06c22d54d: PETALING JAYA: Seorang wanita diperintahkan membayar ganti rugi RM50,000 kepada isteri lelaki yang menjalinkan hubungan sulit dengannya, yang juga seorang wanita lumpuh.

Hakim Johan Lee membenarkan perceraian itu selepas mendapati hubungan sulit suami, keganasan rumah tangga dan tindakan meninggalkan isterinya yang menghidap penyakit serius menjadi 'punca sebenar dan utama' keretakan perkahwinan mereka.

Dalam penghakimannya setebal 47 halaman, Johan berkata wanita yang dinamakan sebagai responden kedua dalam petisyen itu tidak mengamalkan kawalan moral dan secara aktif memikat suami berkenaan sehingga menjauhi isterinya, mengambilnya bekerja, tinggal bersama dengannya serta secara terbuka menunjukkan hubungan mereka ketika bercuti di luar negara.

“Dengan mengambil kira kemudaratan lebih berat yang menjejaskan maruah pempetisyen, mahkamah ini memberikan ganti rugi atas kesalahan zina terhadap responden kedua sebanyak RM50,000, yang perlu dibayar terus kepada pempetisyen menurut Seksyen 58 Akta Membaharui Undang-undang (Perkahwinan dan Perceraian) 1976,” katanya.
Hakim mendapati perbuatan zina itu terbukti berdasarkan imbangan kebarangkalian melalui mesej WhatsApp, rekod perjalanan dan bukti bahawa suami berkenaan serta wanita itu pernah tinggal bersama.
Isteri itu menghidap spinocerebellar ataxia, penyakit neurologi progresif yang tidak boleh diubati sehingga menyebabkannya terlantar, lumpuh dan tidak mampu bercakap.
Ibunya mewakili wanita itu dalam prosiding perceraian berkenaan.
Dalam satu detik menyentuh perasaan yang direkodkan dalam penghakiman itu, ibu wanita berkenaan ditanya mengapa anak perempuannya memerlukan nafkah.
Johan berkata, wanita itu memerlukan bekalan perubatan berterusan, lampin dewasa khusus, fisioterapi dan pengangkutan dengan bantuan.
Beliau memerintahkan suami itu membayar nafkah RM1,500 sebulan bagi menampung penjagaan paliatif isterinya sepanjang hayat wanita berkenaan.

Suami itu turut diperintahkan membayar RM400 sebulan bagi menampung kos penjagaan anak perempuan mereka yang berusia 11 tahun di sebuah pusat jagaan, memasukkan RM300 lagi setiap bulan ke dalam akaun simpanan anak itu serta menanggung semua yuran pendidikan dan perbelanjaan perubatannya sehingga menamatkan pengajian di peringkat pengajian tinggi.

Hak penjagaan dan kawalan anak perempuan itu diberikan kepada pusat jagaan berkenaan dan ibunya. Permohonan untuk bermalam bersama anak ditolak, manakala lawatan pada waktu siang dengan pengawasan oleh kedua-dua ibu bapa tertakluk pada persetujuan anak itu dan kelulusan pusat jagaan.
Suami itu juga diperintahkan membayar RM340,000 kepada isterinya, bersamaan separuh nilai rumah perkahwinan mereka yang dinilai mahkamah sebanyak RM680,000.

Hakim menolak bantahan suami terhadap peranan ibu wanita itu sebagai wakil litigasi anaknya, sambil menegaskan keperluan memudahkan akses kepada keadilan bagi individu yang mengalami ketidakupayaan serius.
Walaupun mahkamah mengambil maklum bukti mengenai kelemahan isteri itu sendiri sepanjang perkahwinan mereka, hakim mendapati salah laku suami merupakan punca utama keretakan rumah tangga.
Perceraian itu diluluskan berkuat kuasa serta-merta. Kedua-dua responden turut diperintahkan membayar kos sebanyak RM50,000.
90c0f3c18bee7691: PETALING JAYA: Choosing a loan usually means comparing interest rates, repayment terms and eligibility rules, then trying to work out which offer actually suits you. Increasingly, Malaysians appear comfortable letting artificial intelligence help with that process.

According to research commissioned by Experian and conducted by Forrester Consulting, 76% of Malaysian respondents said they trusted the accuracy of information provided by large language models when comparing loans.
The study, released last month, surveyed 6,247 credit-active, digitally literate consumers across 13 markets in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.

It found that 57% of Malaysian respondents would allow an AI agent at least some degree of autonomy when applying for a loan or credit card, whether acting after approval, following pre-agreed rules or operating more independently.
This suggests AI could move beyond simply answering questions to helping consumers compare lenders, check eligibility, complete applications and submit authorised documents.

For many respondents, the biggest attraction was saving money and time. Some 92% of Malaysians surveyed believed AI agents could help them find better prices or rates, while 63% said they would be comfortable sharing financial data with one for an automated loan application.

Across the wider 13-market study, 85% believed AI could compare more options than they could manually, while 83% thought it could help them avoid overlooking details such as hidden fees or contract terms.

Experian representative Dawn Lai said consumers here were already changing the way they interacted with financial services. "They are not just experimenting with AI anymore," she said, noting that people were beginning to trust it with more meaningful parts of their financial lives.

Nevertheless, that does not mean Malaysians are ready to hand over every financial decision. The study classified 58% of Malaysian respondents as "agent sceptics", while only 3% were considered "optimisers", indicating considerably greater caution towards granting AI extensive independence.
Trust comes with a very large asterisk

Fraud remains a major concern, with 83% of Malaysian respondents identifying the manipulation of AI agents through fake offers or impersonation by cybercriminals as a key risk. This was the highest level of concern recorded for the issue across the 13 markets surveyed.

That anxiety is understandable given Malaysia's substantial online scam losses. According to home ministry figures, Malaysians lost RM2.97 billion to online fraud in 2025, followed by another RM830 million during the first five months of this year.
As AI tools become increasingly capable of generating convincing text, voices and identities, fraudulent loan offers and impersonation attempts could become more difficult to recognise.
Lai said financial institutions would need to strengthen identity verification, consent mechanisms, fraud prevention and transparency to earn consumers' confidence in AI-assisted financial services.
AI can compare, but should it decide?

There is also an important distinction between using AI to gather information and allowing it to make financial decisions. A loan that appears attractive on paper may still be unsuitable when a borrower's income, existing commitments and repayment horizon are taken into account.
Although AI can compare rates and terms quickly, the reliability of its recommendations depends on the information available and how accurately it interprets the products being assessed.

That distinction helps explain why many respondents appear comfortable with AI as an assistant but remain hesitant about granting it greater control. Across the wider study, 75% said they would feel more comfortable using AI connected to a financial institution they already trusted.

For now, the emerging Malaysian attitude seems to be less "let AI run my finances" and more "help me compare my options, but keep me in the loop". When a decision involves years of repayments, retaining that oversight may be a sensible approach.
7520883903a34c83: PETALING JAYA: A paralysed wife whose husband abandoned her and moved in with another woman has been awarded RM50,000 in damages against the woman for adultery.

Justice Johan Lee granted the divorce after finding that the husband’s affair, domestic violence and abandonment of his severely ill wife were the “true and primary catalysts” for the breakdown of their marriage.

In his 47-page judgment, Johan said the woman, named in the petition as the second respondent, had not exercised moral restraint, and had actively drawn the husband away from his wife, employed him, cohabited with him and flaunted their relationship during overseas holiday trips.

“Having regard to the aggravated injury inflicted upon the petitioner’s dignity, this court awards damages for adultery against the second respondent in the sum of RM50,000, to be paid directly to the petitioner under Section 58 of the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976,” he said.
The judge found that the adultery had been established on a balance of probabilities through WhatsApp messages, travel records and evidence that the husband and the woman had stayed together.
The wife suffers from spinocerebellar ataxia, a progressive and incurable neurological disease that has left her bedridden, paralysed and unable to speak.
Her mother represented her in the divorce proceedings.
In a poignant moment recorded in the judgment, the mother was asked why her daughter needed maintenance.
Her reply was: “Sebab dia nak hidup.” (“Because she wants to live.”)
Johan said the wife required continuous medical supplies, specialised adult diapers, physiotherapy and assisted transport.
He ordered the husband to pay RM1,500 monthly towards her palliative care throughout her lifetime.

The husband was also ordered to pay RM400 monthly towards the upkeep of their 11-year-old daughter at a care centre, deposit another RM300 monthly into the girl’s savings account, and bear all her educational fees and medical expenses until she completes tertiary education.

The daughter’s care and control were placed with the care centre and her mother. Overnight access was refused, while supervised daytime visits by both parents were made subject to the child’s consent and the centre’s approval.
The husband was further ordered to pay the wife RM340,000, representing half the value of their matrimonial home, which the court assessed at RM680,000.
The judge rejected the husband’s challenge to the mother’s role as her daughter’s litigation representative, stressing the need to facilitate access to justice for people with severe disabilities.
Although the court noted evidence of the wife’s own shortcomings during the marriage, it found that the husband’s misconduct was the primary cause of the breakdown.
The divorce was granted with immediate effect. The respondents were also ordered to pay RM50,000 in costs.

3f020a4e3f3780ed: BEIJING: All countries should enjoy freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, China and Djibouti said in a joint statement following a meeting of their foreign ministers in Beijing, expressing concern about the deteriorating security situation.

Djibouti sits on the other side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Yemen, where Iran-backed Houthis have been battling Saudi-backed government forces and seeking to control the whole Yemeni Red Sea coast, disrupting some shipping.

In 2017, China formally opened its first overseas military base in Djibouti. The barren former French colony, which is about the size of Wales, is sandwiched between Ethiopia, Eritrea and Somalia and also hosts US, Japanese and French bases.

The joint statement, released early on Thursday, said both China and Djibouti stressed the importance of maintaining freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and the strait, and "emphasised that the right of merchant ships of all countries to exercise navigation rights in accordance with international law should be respected".

"Both sides believe that in governing and securing the Red Sea, the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and wishes of the Red Sea littoral states should be genuinely respected, avoiding any increase in the overall security risks of the region."

China supports the littoral states of the Red Sea in "constructively maintaining" the safety and smooth flow of international shipping lanes, said the statement, carried by China's official Xinhua news agency.

Neither country wants regional tensions to spill further into the Red Sea, and "major powers outside the region" should respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and avoid resorting to force and unilateral sanctions, it added.

The statement came as the US state department ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia following the escalation of the fighting in Yemen, which has opened another front ​in the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli ⁠war on Iran.
fa59ea89af4cc76b: RAMALLAH: Tentera Israel menahan calon Kongres Demokrat Amerika Syarikat (AS) Brad Lander, yang merupakan sekutu Datuk Bandar New York Zohran Mamdani, bersama puluhan aktivis dan petani Palestin semasa mereka memetik zaitun di Tebing Barat yang diduduki pada Rabu, kata seorang aktivis kepada Anadolu Ajansi.

Aktivis Palestin Amira Muslim memberitahu Anadolu, tentera Israel menahan 45 aktivis warga asing termasuk Lander serta 25 aktivis Israel semasa mereka sedang memetik zaitun di Pekan Husan, barat Bethlehem.

Beliau berkata, pihak berkuasa Israel menahan semua aktivis berkenaan, menempatkan mereka dalam bas dan memindahkan semuanya ke kawasan penempatan berhampiran. Lokasi terakhir dan keberadaan mereka masih belum dipastikan.
Kumpulan itu turut merangkumi aktivis daripada 'T’ruah: The Rabbinic Call for Human Rights', organisasi Yahudi berpangkalan di New York City, kata Amira.
Tiada maklumat lanjut diperoleh secara serta-merta mengenai jumlah petani Palestin yang ditahan atau sama ada tentera Israel telah membebaskan mana-mana individu yang ditahan.
Lander mengesahkan penahanannya menerusi hantaran di platform media sosial X, dengan menyatakan beliau ditahan 'bersama sekumpulan rabbi dan sukarelawan'.
"Kami hanya memetik buah zaitun di dusun berhampiran Nehalim di Tebing Barat," katanya.

Sambil menegaskan sama ada pekerjaan itu merupakan satu jenayah mengikut undang-undang antarabangsa, beliau berkata: "Memetik buah zaitun bukanlah satu jenayah di bawah mana-mana undang-undang yang saya tahu."

Serangan peneroka haram Israel terhadap penduduk Palestin dan tanah mereka di Tebing Barat semakin meningkat semasa musim memetik zaitun. Serangan itu merangkumi pencerobohan fizikal ke atas petani, menghalang mereka daripada mengakses tanah sendiri, mencuri hasil tanaman, dan merosakkan pokok zaitun.
Perangkaan rasmi Palestin menunjukkan kira-kira 750,000 peneroka haram Israel tinggal di Tebing Barat, termasuk Baitulmuqaddis Timur, menerusi 194 penempatan dan kira-kira 400 pos kawalan.
e1cf20d4dfaa5602: WASHINGTON: A crowdsourced verification system used by Elon Musk's X failed to flag a vast majority of false claims related to the US midterm elections - including those promoted by the billionaire - a study said Wednesday.

Community Notes, which allows users to contribute notes that add context or corrections to posts, was introduced by X in late 2022 and the same model is increasingly being adopted by other tech platforms.
But researchers have repeatedly questioned its effectiveness in combating misinformation.

NewsGuard, a US watchdog that rates the credibility of news and information sites, identified dozens of posts on X that advanced false claims related to the elections, including bogus allegations of election fraud.
Only 13 of those posts were tagged with Community Notes.
"X's crowdsourced fact-checking programme failed to flag 93.1% of false claims related to the US midterm elections," NewsGuard said.
"The uncorrected X posts have drawn millions of interactions ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections."

The falsehoods included a post by a conservative commentator claiming that New York and California had made it illegal for voters to show - and officials to ask for - their voter ID. No such rule exists in either Democratic stronghold.
Musk has often promoted Community Notes, calling it "awesome" and asserting that all users, including himself, were subject to being corrected by the crowd-sourced model.
NewsGuard, however, said that Musk, who has 241.5 million followers on X, has advanced at least four false claims related to the midterm elections, none of which carried Community Notes.
X did not respond to AFP's request for comment.
Studies have shown Community Notes can work to dispel some falsehoods, like vaccine misinformation, but researchers have long cautioned that it works best for topics where there is broad consensus.
Some researchers have also cautioned that Community Notes users can be motivated to target political opponents by partisan beliefs.
Tech platforms increasingly view the community-driven model as an alternative to professional fact-checking.

Last year, Meta ended its third-party fact-checking programme in the United States, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg saying it had led to "too much censorship." Professional fact-checkers vehemently reject the claim.
Last month, Meta said it had begun testing its own version of Community Notes in 16 Spanish-speaking countries in Latin America, in a step toward replacing its fact-checking program.
Meta gave no timeline for when the change will become official.
Meta's Oversight Board, a quasi-independent body the company funds to review its moderation decisions, said Community Notes was not an adequate replacement for fact-checking.
AFP currently works in 26 languages with Meta's global fact-checking program, including in Latin America.
bc3c865c38f252bf: KUALA LUMPUR: International conflicts, geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty have made stock investing increasingly challenging. Wars, trade disputes, sanctions, disruptions to energy supplies and strained relations between major powers can unsettle financial markets and undermine investor confidence. Share prices may fluctuate sharply, sometimes in response to events that have little immediate impact on the underlying businesses.

In such turbulent times, investors must recognise that successful investing is not about predicting every geopolitical development. It is about making rational decisions, managing risks and remaining focused on the long-term fundamentals of the businesses in which they invest.
Understand the Difference Between Uncertainty and Permanent Damage

Stock markets dislike uncertainty. When international conflicts escalate, investors may sell shares out of fear that economic growth will slow, inflation will rise or corporate earnings will deteriorate. However, a falling share price does not automatically mean that a company's intrinsic value has declined by the same proportion.

Investors must distinguish between temporary market anxiety and permanent damage to a business. A company with strong finances, recurring revenues, a competitive advantage and resilient demand may withstand geopolitical turbulence better than its share price initially suggests.

Conversely, some businesses may suffer lasting consequences from prolonged conflicts, particularly those dependent on disrupted supply chains, vulnerable export markets or volatile commodity prices. The important question is not simply whether a share price has fallen, but whether the company's long-term earnings power and financial position have fundamentally changed.
Focus on Financial Strength and Cash Flow

During uncertain periods, financially sound businesses become particularly valuable. Investors should examine a company's debt levels, cash reserves, operating cash flow, interest obligations and ability to generate profits under adverse conditions.

Companies carrying excessive debt may struggle when borrowing costs rise or revenues decline. Businesses with weak cash generation may be forced to borrow, raise new capital or cut dividends at precisely the wrong time.

Cash flow deserves special attention because reported accounting profits do not necessarily translate into cash available to meet obligations. A company that consistently converts earnings into cash is generally better positioned to survive economic shocks, maintain operations and seize opportunities when weaker competitors retreat.
Maintain a Margin of Safety
Uncertainty increases the importance of valuation discipline. Even an excellent company can become a poor investment if purchased at an excessive price.

A margin of safety means buying a share at a meaningful discount to a conservatively estimated intrinsic value. This provides some protection against errors in analysis, unexpected economic developments and further deterioration in business conditions.

When markets fall, investors should not assume that every declining share has become cheap. Some prices fall because the market is excessively pessimistic; others fall because the underlying business is genuinely deteriorating. Careful analysis is essential to distinguish between these situations.
Diversify Without Diluting Investment Quality

Diversification helps reduce the damage caused by an adverse event affecting a particular company, industry or country. Investors should avoid excessive concentration in businesses exposed to the same geopolitical risks.

For Malaysian investors, this means considering exposure to domestic demand, export markets, currencies, commodity prices and international supply chains. Different industries respond differently to global disruptions. Energy producers may benefit from higher oil prices, while transport companies and energy-intensive manufacturers may face rising costs.

Nevertheless, diversification should not become an excuse to own businesses that are poorly understood or financially weak. A portfolio of carefully selected, financially resilient companies is preferable to indiscriminate diversification.
Keep Cash and Avoid Emotional Decisions

Holding some cash can provide flexibility during periods of uncertainty. It also allows investors to take advantage of attractive opportunities without being forced to sell existing investments at depressed prices.

However, holding excessive cash indefinitely has its own costs, including inflation and the potential loss of long-term investment returns. The appropriate allocation depends on investment objectives, time horizon, liquidity requirements and risk tolerance.

Investors should also avoid excessive leverage and margin financing. Borrowing to invest magnifies losses and may force the sale of shares during market declines, leaving investors unable to benefit from a subsequent recovery.
Adopt a Long-Term Perspective

History demonstrates that markets have endured wars, recessions, financial crises and political upheavals. Although past recoveries do not guarantee future outcomes, businesses that remain competitive and financially sound can continue creating value despite a difficult external environment.

Long-term investors should review their holdings regularly, but not confuse activity with progress. If the fundamentals remain intact and the valuation remains reasonable, temporary volatility may be something to tolerate rather than fear.
Conclusion

In the final analysis, uncertainty is an unavoidable feature of investing. The greatest advantage an investor can possess is not the ability to predict the future, but the discipline to make sound decisions when the future is uncertain.

784add22d2a0ca5a: KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Malaysia's next challenge is turning investment into sustainable growth, higher-value jobs and stronger local businesses, industry experts said.
The Johor economic corridor marks its 20th anniversary this year with RM525.26 billion in cumulative investments, surpassing its original RM383 billion target by RM142.26 billion.
Industry experts said the focus now is on building a more advanced industrial base, improving liveability and helping Malaysian companies secure a bigger role in regional and global supply chains.

Zerin Properties founder and chief executive officer Previndran Singhe said Iskandar Malaysia's investment performance reflected the sustained efforts of the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) and the Johor government.

"This has been a long time coming, and I welcome it. When Iskandar was launched in 2006, plenty of people in our industry, myself included, wondered how long it would take to gain real traction, said Previndran who has more than 35 years of experience in the property industry,
"RM525 billion later, with over a million jobs created and household incomes more than doubled, the answer is clear. IRDA and the Johor government deserve the credit," he told Business Times.
However, he said the next phase would be more demanding, as attracting investment alone would not guarantee that Iskandar Malaysia became a compelling place to live, work and build businesses.
"Attracting capital is one thing. Building places people actually want to live in is another," he said.

Previndran said companies and skilled professionals increasingly considered quality of life alongside office costs, rental rates and other conventional investment factors when deciding where to establish operations or build careers.

A young engineer or regional executive choosing between Johor and another regional destination would also consider access to parks, cafés, cultural activities, reliable public transport and shorter commuting times, he said.
"Investors follow talent, and talent goes where life is good. Those everyday things matter more than any brochure," he said.
He said Iskandar Malaysia already had considerable advantages, including its waterfront, marinas, the historic character of Johor Bahru's old town, green spaces and a young population.
However, better public transport, more coordinated urban planning and stronger community amenities would be necessary to make the region more attractive to residents and investors over the long term.

The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is expected to transform cross-border mobility, but its benefits would depend partly on how effectively commuters could connect to destinations beyond the rail stations.

"The RTS Link will change how people move between Johor Baru and Singapore, but if you step off the train and the only way forward is a Grab or your own car, we have missed the point," Previndran said, calling for reliable bus services, a proper rapid transit network, and shaded walkways and cycling paths linking townships.
He also highlighted the need for closer coordination among local authorities, particularly in planning approvals, infrastructure delivery and township management.

More vibrant neighbourhoods, with independent cafés, bookshops, small businesses, weekend markets and cultural activities, could help give Johor Bahru a stronger urban identity and encourage more visitors from Singapore to spend time in the city beyond shopping and refuelling, he said.
Sustainability should also be incorporated into future development through greener buildings, more trees, improved drainage and inclusive communities designed to serve different generations.
"Iskandar has shown the world it can bring in investment. The next 20 years will be about making it a place people are proud to call home," he said.

Olive Tree Property Consultants founder and chief executive officer Samuel Tan said Iskandar Malaysia's next phase of growth would depend on how effectively it leveraged its strategic location and the complementary strengths of Johor and Singapore, particularly through the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

The JS-SEZ aims to strengthen economic integration between the two jurisdictions by combining Johor's land availability, industrial capacity, talent pool and competitive operating costs with Singapore's international capital, technology, business networks and access to global markets.
The zone attracted RM76.98 billion in approved investments in 2025, highlighting Johor's appeal as a complementary base for companies seeking to expand their regional operations.

Tan said the opportunity was significant, but realising its full potential would require close coordination between the two governments, particularly in infrastructure planning, energy security, workforce development and cross-border mobility.

Streamlined customs and immigration procedures, alongside stronger physical and digital connectivity, would also be essential to reducing operating costs and enabling businesses to move goods, people and services more efficiently across the border.
"The JS-SEZ creates a significant advantage by bringing together complementary strengths that no single jurisdiction could offer in isolation.

"This includes Johor's abundant land, established industrial capacity, growing talent pool and competitive operating expenses, alongside Singapore's global capital networks, technology, business services and access to international markets," he told Business Times.
The need to translate investment momentum into tangible economic outcomes is also reflected in the government's broader efforts to develop strategic industrial and logistics hubs.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat earlier this month, said Sedenak Nexus in the northern part of the JS-SEZ had the potential to attract RM12 billion in investments and create 45,000 jobs.

He also said the government would continue strengthening special border economic zones, with trade along the Bukit Kayu Hitam-Sadao corridor reaching RM27 billion in the first six months of this year.
One initiative is the development of the 49.37-hectare NCT InnoSphere as a heavy vehicle, engineering, maintenance and logistics hub serving industries in Kulim and Penang.
According to IRDA, Iskandar Malaysia has generated more than one million jobs and more than doubled average household incomes since its establishment.

However, with competition for investment intensifying across Asean, the region faces growing pressure to move beyond attracting capital and build a more productive economic ecosystem that generates skilled employment, strengthens domestic supply chains and enables Malaysian companies to capture a greater share of the value created.
IRDA said its next development phase would prioritise advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, modern logistics, and high-value financial and business services.

"Emphasis will be placed on increasing productivity and high-value economic activity, including advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, and logistics, as well as financial and business services," it said in a statement on Tuesday.

The authority said its strategy would extend beyond headline investment figures to encompass technology transfer, domestic business participation, local innovation and the ability of Malaysian enterprises to move up the global value chain.

Deputy Prime Minister II and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said Iskandar Malaysia's next phase must be measured by the quality and sustainability of its economic gains, rather than investment figures alone.
Fadillah chaired the 36th IRDA Governing Council meeting on behalf of Anwar, alongside Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.

"The next phase should be assessed not only by the total investment attracted but also by the quality of opportunities created, the strength of the economic ecosystem, and the long-term benefits that businesses and communities can enjoy," he said.

IRDA said land availability and competitive costs, once major considerations for investors, were no longer sufficient to guarantee competitiveness as businesses increasingly assessed infrastructure readiness, energy reliability, skilled labour availability and digital connectivity.
The efficiency of cross-border movement for goods and people, together with access to regional and international markets, had also become increasingly important in investment decisions.

21c37ee597563891: KOTA KINABALU: The toll-free Pan Borneo Highway was envisioned as a major transport link connecting Sabah, Sarawak and Brunei. But more than a decade after its launch, progress in the two East Malaysian states has diverged sharply.
As of March 31, the Auditor General's Report 2/2026 found that Sarawak had completed 10 of its 11 work packages, with the remaining package, WP11, 99.9 per cent complete.
In Sabah, only four of the 35 work packages under Phase 1, which spans 706km, had been completed.
Of the remaining packages, nine were classified as sick projects, 13 were delayed and nine were ahead of schedule.
A total of RM10.547 billion of the RM11.153 billion allocated for Sabah's highway project had been spent, yet the project remains significantly behind schedule.
The completion deadline has since been extended to 2030 due to weaknesses in project planning.

Public Accounts Committee chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin has warned that the project risks remaining incomplete due to a funding shortfall unless the government approves additional allocations.
WHY IS SARAWAK'S PORTION PROGRESSING WELL?
In 2024, former Sabah Works Minister Datuk Shahelmey Yahya said Sarawak had arranged sukuk financing early to ensure sufficient funds for all its Pan Borneo Highway packages.

According to DanaInfra Nasional Berhad's website, the infrastructure financing entity was mandated in July 2015 to raise funds to part-finance Phase 1 of the Sarawak Pan Borneo Highway, with financing of up to RM13 billion backed by a government guarantee.
The financing programme was expanded to RM15.8 billion in May 2023 to meet the remaining construction funding requirements.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi also credited Building Information Modelling (BIM) technology with saving RM157 million and averting a potential 10-year delay to the Sarawak project.
The MP for Kapit said the technology helped resolve more than 3,000 drawing errors during construction in 2016.
WHY IS SABAH'S PAN BORNEO HIGHWAY FACING DELAYS?

Sabah Deputy Chief Minister and Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said this year that the project had been affected by the termination of the previous project delivery partner (PDP) model in 2019.
The switch to the conventional implementation model left the project dependent on annual federal allocations.
Dr Gunsalam said most contractor appointments for the new packages were finalised only between February 2024 and January 2026, after the federal government reconsidered the implementation method.
Land acquisition has also held up construction, with the state government allowing landowners to appeal against compensation offers.
Shortages of bitumen, stone and manpower have also contributed to the delays.

Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan previously told Parliament that other factors included contractor performance, weather conditions, utility relocation, the Covid-19 pandemic and weaknesses in project governance.

0ddb6fab8aa4655d: KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) has tightened training grant approvals, stepped up programme verification and strengthened investment safeguards as part of a sweeping reform to address governance weaknesses and restore stakeholder confidence.

Its chief executive, Datuk Shamir Aziz, said the organisation has introduced stricter application requirements, as well as increased physical and digital checks on training programmes and overhauled procurement procedures following findings in the Auditor General's Report 2024.

Since June, training applications must be submitted at least 14 days before a programme begins, ending retrospective approvals and giving HRD Corp more time to scrutinise documents and ensure compliance.
The Auditor General's Report 2024 had flagged 62 levy applications worth RM1.68 million that were approved after training had taken place.
It also highlighted questionable applications involving repeated participant information and training facilities that did not correspond with approved specifications.
Shamir, who was appointed to the role in January, is at the heart of the sweeping reforms, which aims to close loopholes while ensuring employers can continue to access training support.

"I inherited a heavy ledger of broken trust. Entrusted with the levies of over 109,000 employers funding 5.4 million Malaysian workers, it is my promise to restore trust and integrity in HRD Corp," he said.

Since the 14-day advance application policy took effect, HRD Corp has received 137,460 applications under its HRD Corp Claimable Courses scheme for in-house training and public programmes, an increase of nearly 12 per cent over the same period last year.
However, the approval rate fell to 78.8 per cent from 93.1 per cent last year, which Shamir attributed to more rigorous screening under the reformed process.
"Retrospective training approvals are a thing of the past. All training sessions must now be applied for at least 14 days beforehand.
"This policy allows HRD Corp ample time to rigorously check paperwork and approve training in accordance with its procedures, leaving virtually no room for manipulation."

The manufacturing sector accounted for the largest share of approvals at 26 per cent, followed by wholesale and retail at 14 per cent, professional and technical services at 12 per cent and construction at eight per cent.
HRD Corp has also significantly increased checks to establish whether approved training programmes are actually conducted.
The agency verified 6,231 training programmes last year. Between June and September this year, it verified 19,322 sessions.
"That is roughly three times the previous year's total, achieved in just four months," said Shamir.
To address staffing limitations, more than 15,000 training sessions were verified digitally, while 3,500 underwent physical inspection.
Nonetheless, the agency aims to achieve 100 per cent verification of training programmes.

Shamir said HRD Corp was developing a system incorporating MyDigital ID, QR codes, geotagging and timestamps to verify attendance, with a pilot planned for next year and full implementation targeted for 2028.
FUNDS MANAGED WITH DISCIPLINE AND INTEGRITY
Despite the tighter controls, HRD Corp continued to disburse funds to employers, paying RM1.4 billion across 335,877 approved claims since January.
"This figure represents the 335,877 decisions by employers to invest in their people, and HRD Corp stood behind every one of them," Shamir said.
ACCOUNTABILITY AND INVESTMENT SAFEGUARDS

Shamir said internal reviews into four critical areas — the management of unutilised levies, the acquisition of Menara Ikhlas, investment management and the overdue RM14 million procurement of the New Core System — had led to action against its personnel.
Six senior officers were suspended from their positions this year and they are no longer with the organisation. Three of them were subsequently dismissed.
"Accountability is where reform begins, not where it ends. I was brought in to clean up HRD Corp and that is exactly what I intend to do. There will be no tolerance for failures of accountability.
"Every ringgit entrusted to us belongs to Malaysian employers and workers. We will ensure it is managed with the discipline and integrity they deserve," Shamir said.
HRD Corp is also working to address concerns over investments made between 2020 and 2024, when part of its funds was invested in high-risk instruments without adequate safeguards.
Shamir said RM447.2 million had been recovered.
"The remaining exposure is down to RM396.3 million, or 8.6 per cent of total investment funds, and legal action to recover the rest is ongoing. This episode cannot repeat itself."
He said investments were permitted under the Human Resources Development Act 2001 and were necessary to sustain the organisation's operations and staff salaries.
"The four per cent service fee, event revenue and other income are simply insufficient to sustain HRD Corp's vast operations, especially to support three million training opportunities in 2027."
Moving forward, all investments must be backed by collateral equivalent to 110 per cent of the investment, excluding shares.
"Put simply, if an investment fails, we can claim assets worth more than we invested," Shamir said.
RAISED BY AUDITOR GENERAL ADDRESSED
Of the 10 issues raised in the Auditor General's Report 2024, four were resolved last year, five remain on the auditor general's dashboard for continued monitoring and one was being addressed.
HRD Corp also appointed five new board members in February, bringing expertise in retail, Islamic finance, manufacturing, export markets, energy and cooperatives.
Shamir said the board's diverse experience would strengthen checks and balances, protect public trust and support skills development among Malaysian workers.
PROCUREMENT OVERHAUL AND TRAINING PRIORITIES

The RM14 million New Core System, a digital platform procured by HRD Corp, had fallen years behind schedule and failed user-acceptance testing three times, prompting changes to procurement procedures.
Shamir said all procurement exercises now went through open tender and were assessed by three committees comprising members from different departments.
For smaller purchases, the lowest bid would no longer automatically prevail, with quality, delivery and value also taken into account.
Tender periods had also been extended from seven to 21 days in line with Finance Ministry guidelines.
"A fair process is not a favour we grant. It is an obligation we owe."
TRAINING FRAMEWORK REVIEW
With the governance reforms underway, HRD Corp is also reviewing its training framework to better meet employers' needs and align skills development with industry requirements.
The organisation has engaged more than 500 employers, training providers and industry associations as it revises its Allowable Cost Matrix.
Consultations will continue until the end of the year and stakeholders are encouraged to provide feedback.

Training schemes are being regrouped around high-impact areas, with greater emphasis on professional certification to support Malaysia's target of having 35 per cent of its workforce classified as skilled by 2030.
HRD Corp is also working to make Continuing Professional Development points for professionals claimable under the revised framework.
"Our primary focus is our stakeholders, the employers and those who contribute to the fund. We want to know what employers need; they are our priority.
"We have a plan. We know it's not perfect, but we will keep striving for better," said Shamir.
Next year, HRD Corp aims to make company-sponsored educational degrees a claimable benefit from levy accounts.
To boost retention beyond just tax exemptions, employers will be able to use their levies as scholarships to upskill staff.
"We foresee that as soon as next year, job advertisements will prominently feature scholarships." he said.
PROFESSIONALISING THE CARE SECTOR
HRD Corp's expanded role in skills development will also include efforts to professionalise the caregiving sector and create opportunities for women and other groups seeking employment.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced a RM40 million allocation for HRD Corp's Madani Professional Caregiver initiative under the 2027 Budget on Oct 9.
The programme aims to train up to 8,000 people, including homemakers, housewives, school leavers, technical and vocational education and training graduates and jobseekers.
Shamir said the initiative would recognise the skills required in caregiving and help establish clearer standards in the sector.
"Caring for the elderly or disabled is highly skilled, demanding work. It deserves proper training, clear standards, and fair wages."
He thanked the prime minister and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan for their support, as well as HRD Corp employees for their contributions to the reform process.
"HRD Corp belongs to the employers and workers of Malaysia. We hold every ringgit in trust for them.
"We have not finished keeping that promise, but we are keeping it, day by day, claim by claim, ringgit by ringgit.
"The work will continue."

e4567578085835ad: PETALING JAYA: Kontroversi khalwat membabitkan Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad dijangka tidak banyak menjejaskan sokongannya dalam kalangan penyokong Bersama, yang cenderung memisahkan kehidupan peribadi seseorang ahli politik daripada rekod politiknya, kata penganalisis.
Namun, mereka berkata isu itu mungkin menyukarkan parti serpihan PKR berkenaan menarik sokongan pengundi Melayu konservatif ketika Bersama cuba meluaskan asas sokongannya.

James Chin daripada Universiti Tasmania berkata, kontroversi itu tidak semestinya menamatkan kerjaya politik Nik Nazmi kerana penyokong parti berbilang kaum lazimnya dapat membezakan antara kehidupan peribadi dan prestasi politik seseorang pemimpin.
“Tidak, ini bukan pengakhiran kerjaya politiknya,” katanya kepada FMT.

Chin berkata, beberapa ahli politik sebelum ini berjaya meneruskan kerjaya selepas berdepan kontroversi seumpama itu, dengan memberi contoh Presiden Amanah Mohamad Sabu dan bekas presiden MCA Dr Chua Soi Lek.

Mohamad, yang ketika itu pemimpin Pemuda PAS, didakwa berkhalwat pada 1995 tetapi dibebaskan Mahkamah Syariah Kelantan tanpa dipanggil membela diri selepas pihak pendakwaan gagal membuktikan kes prima facie. Pada 2011, beliau dipilih sebagai timbalan presiden PAS.
Chua pula meletakkan semua jawatan dalam kerajaan dan parti pada 2008 susulan skandal seks, namun kembali aktif dalam politik dua tahun kemudian apabila memenangi jawatan presiden MCA.
Menurut Chin, perkembangan itu menunjukkan seseorang ahli politik masih berpeluang untuk kembali selepas berdepan kontroversi.
“Banyak bergantung kepada parti mana anda datang. Jika dari PAS, mungkin sukar untuk kembali, tetapi jika dari DAP atau PKR, ia sebenarnya tidak begitu menjadi masalah,” katanya.

Nik Nazmi, yang juga pemimpin bersama Bersama, mengesahkan pada Sabtu bahawa beliau dan seorang wanita ditahan Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor (Jais) di Petaling Jaya pada 15 Okt kerana disyaki berkhalwat.
Susulan kejadian itu, bekas Ahli Parlimen Setiawangsa berkenaan digantung keahlian oleh Bersama selama tiga bulan.

Syaza Shukri daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia turut berpandangan, kontroversi itu tidak mungkin memberi kesan politik berpanjangan terhadap Nik Nazmi, walaupun isu seumpama itu boleh menjejaskan seseorang ahli politik dalam jangka pendek, terutama jika berlaku hampir dengan pilihan raya.

Katanya, skandal berkaitan dakwaan hubungan seksual lazimnya menimbulkan sensitiviti lebih besar dalam kalangan pengundi Melayu berbanding skandal kewangan kerana ia sering dikaitkan dengan soal “maruah dan kehormatan” seseorang pemimpin.

Menurut Syaza, cabaran lebih besar bagi Bersama ialah menarik pengundi Melayu baharu dan bukannya mengekalkan penyokong sedia ada kerana parti itu sememangnya belum mempunyai asas sokongan Melayu yang besar.

“Insiden ini akan menyukarkan mereka menarik pengundi Melayu yang masih belum membuat keputusan,” katanya, sambil menambah Bersama dijangka tidak berdepan masalah besar mengekalkan penyokong sedia ada.
Sokongan keluarga pengaruhi peluang kembali
Kedua-dua penganalisis turut berkata peluang Nik Nazmi untuk kembali aktif dalam politik mungkin dipengaruhi reaksi keluarganya terhadap kontroversi itu.
Chin berkata, peluang bekas menteri persekutuan itu untuk bangkit semula lebih baik sekiranya keluarganya terus memberikan sokongan.
“Selagi keluarga berdiam diri dan tiada siapa bercakap mengenainya, perkara itu akan dimaafkan,” kata Syaza.
Katanya, sokongan terbuka daripada isteri Nik Nazmi juga boleh membantu beliau mendapatkan semula kepercayaan orang ramai.
Syaza berkata, pengundi berhak menilai tingkah laku peribadi ahli politik, namun mereka juga wajar memberi peluang kepada seseorang pemimpin untuk memperbaiki keadaan.
“Saya rasa pengundi akan memaafkan, terutama jika beliau mengambil langkah yang betul.”
3e624b3c0fb4c45d: PETALING JAYA: Yin Wen Choi always knew she wanted a corgi, but she also hoped to adopt a rescue dog. Little did she know that those two wishes would come together in one particularly sassy package - Coco.
In June 2025, Choi and her partner Aaron Lau saw a Facebook adoption post about Coco whose previous owner reportedly gave her up after moving to a condominium with a no-pet policy.
Lau contacted the fosterer immediately, and what began as a spontaneous decision turned into a new chapter for the trio.
“It felt as though everything had fallen into place and Coco was meant to be ours,” Choi told FMT Lifestyle.
When the couple took the three-year-old to the vet on adoption day, they discovered she had kidney and gallbladder stones.

“The vet told us that the stones were quite large and might have developed over the course of a year. That meant she could have been suffering in silence for some time, because she was peeing blood,” shared Lau.
With proper treatment, Coco recovered from her health problems. However, as with many rescue dogs, adjusting to her new home was not always easy.
“When I first brought Coco home, she had mild separation anxiety. Whenever we weren’t around, she would whine, pant and walk around in circles,” Lau said.

Coco also struggled with reactivity towards other dogs during walks, sometimes barking loudly or excitedly lunging at them. Lau began training her, and while there are still occasional setbacks, he said Coco improved and is now composed about 90% of the time.

“Our neighbours knew her for her loud barking,” he said. “Now, each time we bring her to the park, she’s a better version of herself. It has taken a lot of blood, sweat and tears - literally, in some cases,” he laughed.
Unsurprisingly, Coco has grown closest to Lau. The couple said she has plenty of quirks and sass to keep them laughing.

“Corgis are known for their judgemental looks and signature side-eye, and Coco definitely has that expression,” Choi said. Lau added that Coco could maintain an intense stare for minutes when she wanted something, whether it was permission to leave her feeding cage or simply get their attention.

Her sassiness extends to mealtimes, too. Coco is a picky eater who detests drinking water, prompting Choi to add water or broth to her kibble. Sometimes, she even needs hand-feeding before agreeing to eat.
But her cheeky antics are not always so harmless. Although toilet-trained, she occasionally pees in a particular spot in the living room when left alone.
“When we return, she’ll either give us the most guilty-looking puppy eyes or hide in another room. She knows she’s done something wrong,” Lau said.

Coco has also brought the couple comfort and companionship. Choi created an Instagram account for her soon after the adoption, just to document her life and share her cuteness with others. “People often tell us Coco is lucky, but we're lucky to have her too,” said Lau.

Choi added: “Coco has been a blessing to me. When I’m stressed after work, just seeing her can bring my stress levels down to zero. At the same time, I know that losing her one day will be my biggest heartbreak.”
Both hope Coco’s transformation will encourage others to consider adoption, even if they have their hearts set on a particular breed.
“Coco has reinforced my belief that you can adopt a dog regardless of its age,” said Lau.

Choi added: “Corgis are known to be stubborn, but Coco has shown us how much a dog can improve with time, patience and training. If she can make such progress, I'm sure many other dogs can too, regardless of their breed.”
